detailed_rationale:
Jupiter Wagons (formerly Commercial Engineers & Body Builders Co.) rode the FY22-FY24 Indian Railways wagon-ordering supercycle to very strong growth, but that cycle is now decisively normalizing. Q4 FY26 sales of Rs.780cr and net profit of Rs.27cr compare to Rs.1,045cr/Rs.103cr in Q4 FY25 - a roughly 25% revenue decline and 74% profit decline year-on-year, consistent with the quant model's -26.5% trailing 1-year revenue growth flag (versus +12.1% 3-year CAGR, a genuine growth-divergence). Operating margin has compressed to around 10% in the latest quarter, well below the mid-teens the company posted during the wagon boom. Working-capital quality is also deteriorating: debtor days rose from 73 to 97 and overall working-capital days from 74 to 119, while gross debt has climbed to roughly Rs.996cr. ROE has fallen to 6.4% and ROCE to 9.2% (TTM), a sharp step-down from the ~18-20% ROE the company reported during the FY23-24 peak.

The business itself is not broken - Jupiter Wagons is India's largest 25-tonne wagon manufacturer and has diversified into road/multimodal mobility (tankers, containers, brake systems, EV light commercial vehicles), which provides some offset to the railway order-book normalization. But at a trailing P/E near 62x against ROE of just 6.4% and a still-declining revenue run-rate, the market is pricing in a re-acceleration that the latest quarters are not delivering. Promoter holding has also declined about 4 points over three years (68.3% now), a mild but real governance-adjacent signal alongside the earnings deceleration.

Reverse-DCF: a 62x multiple on a capital-goods/rail-supplier business implies the market expects a return to high-teens-or-better growth with margin recovery. Given the order book is normalizing off a supercycle peak and new capacity (including competitors like Titagarh, Texmaco, BEML) has entered wagon manufacturing, that re-acceleration is not evident in the numbers - this screens as a cyclical peak-multiple problem, not a temporary dip.
recommendation_rationale: The quant model already flags this a Sell on both the 3-year (38.3) and 1-year (32.0) composite scores, and my own read of the numbers - decelerating revenue, compressing margins, deteriorating working capital, falling ROE, and a still-rich 62x multiple - confirms rather than contradicts that call. There is no balance-sheet cheapness or defensive quality (like GNFC's net-cash position) to offset the growth/valuation mismatch here, so this is a straightforward confirmation, not a rescue candidate.
summary: Jupiter Wagons benefited hugely from the recent Indian Railways wagon-ordering boom, but that cycle is now normalizing: the latest quarter showed revenue and profit down sharply year-on-year, margins compressing, and working capital (debtor and inventory days) stretching out. Despite this deceleration, the stock still trades at a rich ~62x trailing earnings and returns on capital have fallen to single digits. We see this as a cyclical capital-goods story past its peak, priced for growth it is not currently delivering, and recommend continuing to treat it as a Sell.
positive_para: Jupiter Wagons remains India's largest manufacturer of 25-tonne wagons with a roughly 25% share of a still-structurally-growing wagon market (rail freight modal-share push, dedicated freight corridor ramp-up, continuing private wagon investment scheme), and it has diversified into road/multimodal mobility (tankers, fire engines, EV LCVs, brake systems) which reduces pure-play exposure to the railway ordering cycle. FII holding has been rising (2.3% to 4.2% over three years) even as promoter stake has trimmed slightly, suggesting some institutional interest persists through the current slowdown.
negative_para: The bear case is straightforward and, in our view, currently winning: revenue fell roughly 25% and profit roughly 74% year-on-year in the latest quarter, margins have compressed to about 10% from historically higher levels, and working capital is deteriorating (debtor days 73 to 97, WC days 74 to 119) even as debt has grown to near Rs.1,000cr. ROE of 6.4% and ROCE of 9.2% no longer justify a 62x earnings multiple. This has the hallmarks of a post-supercycle normalization in railway wagon capex, with new manufacturing capacity (competitors) also crowding into pricing, and there is no valuation cushion (rich, not cheap) to protect against further deceleration.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~62x trailing P/E on a capital-goods supplier implies the market still expects sustained double-digit growth with margin recovery. The latest results show the opposite trajectory (revenue -25% YoY, margins down, ROE at 6.4%), so the current multiple looks to be pricing a return to supercycle-era growth that the order book does not currently support. We read this as rich, not cheap, on a normalized-earnings basis.
